rationale: C06 plausibly supplied the child’s immediate drafting frame. Both are short executive orders headed “Section 1. Emergency Authority” and begin with the distinctive construction “To provide additional authority to [the Secretaries] to respond to the national emergency declared by [reference], the authority/authorities ... are invoked and made available, according to [their] terms.” Both then specify how the delegated emergency authority may be exercised and end with a consultation requirement. C02 is a strong substantive antecedent because it invokes the same 19 U.S.C. 1318 emergency authority for Treasury to extend customs deadlines during a national emergency, but its proclamation form and detailed warehouse provisions are less textually and structurally proximate. C05 uses closely related invocation language and an operative follow-on direction, but concerns military border authorities rather than customs deadlines.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Section 1. Emergency Authority. (a) To provide additional authority to the Secretary of the Treasury (Secretary) to respond to the national emergency declared by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE]
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Section 1. Emergency Authority. To provide additional authority to the Secretaries of Defense and Homeland Security to respond to the national emergency declared by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE]
shared_material.explanation: Identical section heading and highly distinctive opening sentence structure strongly indicate reuse.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the authority at section 1318(a) of title 19, United States Code ... is invoked and made available, according to its terms, to the Secretary
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the authorities under section 12302 of title 10, United States Code, and sections 2127, 2308, 2314, and 3735 of title 14, United States Code, are invoked and made available, according to their terms, to the Secretaries of Defense and Homeland Security
shared_material.explanation: The same statutory-invocation formula is adapted by substituting the relevant statute and recipient.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Secretary shall consult with the Secretary of Homeland Security or his designee before exercising ... any of the authority
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Secretary of Defense or the Secretary of Homeland Security, as applicable, will ensure appropriate consultation is undertaken ... with respect to the utilization ... under this authority
shared_material.explanation: Both orders conclude their compact delegation machinery with a consultation safeguard tied to use of the invoked authority.
